question: When would you bypass an ORM and write SQL or a query builder for a Nest API?
shortAnswer: Complex reporting, performance-critical joins, or queries the ORM expresses poorly—while still parameterizing.
strongAnswer: ORMs excel at CRUD and simple relations but can hide N+1 issues and awkward SQL. For analytical queries, careful join strategies, or verified EXPLAIN plans, query builders/raw SQL are appropriate. Keep transactions at the use-case layer and never concatenate user input into SQL.
commonWrongAnswer: Never write SQL if an ORM exists.
productionRelevance: Avoids production slowdowns from naive ORM usage.
